data.narrative:
Lace Lithography is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Bodil Holst and Adria Salvador Palau. The company has raised $60M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in chips and semiconductors, with particular relevance to same-stage privates: SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression anchors on the $60M raised as a proxy for current value, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yielding $120M. Peer-median across the 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables produces $2.3B, with a range of $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S (median 20.5x across the three public tickers) cannot be applied absent the target's revenue disclosure. Triangulation across the two viable methods produces a low of $102M, median of $1.2B, and high of $2.7B.

The wide spread between stage-progression and peer-median reflects material uncertainty around whether Lace's technology and market position align with median-tier peers or outlier valuations like SambaNova. Revenue trajectory, IP defensibility, and customer traction are critical to narrowing this range.
